statements.r5-m03: The top-8 singular directions per layer matrix of the Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math weight change act like the opening cue: they switch the base into the deliberative 'Okay' register and nothing more, without RL's longer checking policy. So base + top8 on the plain prompt writes answers of the cued base's length and makes the cued base's quick finished-wrong errors, and adding the cue on top of top8 adds almost nothing.
statements.r5-m03-rival: The top-8 edit is an incomplete switch that happens or fails sample by sample. On most answers (about 85-90 %) it puts the base on a weak dose of RL's own policy: longer answers, RL-style checking, almost no quick wrong answers, errors only on hard problems. On the other 10-15 % the plain prompt leaves the base in its plain-base register: short answers, wrong about half the time whatever the problem's difficulty. So top8 plain is a mixture of RL-like answers and plain-base answers, not a copy of the cued base.

experiments.why: The mechanism puts quick wrong answers in a short plain-base register that is wrong about half the time regardless of difficulty, so removing those votes should let the deliberative samples decide; since the cue already switches most cued-base samples, few are that short and the gain over the plain 446 vote is at most a few problems.

other_prediction.why: Under r5-m03 the cued base's quick finished-wrong answers are only a few percent of its short answers (13 wrong of 263 at <= 2,000 tokens), so answers of <= 600 tokens are mostly right; dropping them removes about as many right votes as wrong ones, and the score stays near the plain 4-vote 446 instead of rising toward pass@4 467.
